checks.message: IMDSv2 not enforced
checks.context: Without this, any process running on the instance (including malware) can steal the attached IAM role credentials with a single curl command — no authentication required.

checks.message: Root volume encryption not specified
checks.context: Unencrypted EBS volumes can be detached and mounted on another instance, exposing all data at rest. Encryption is free and has no performance impact on modern instance types. The device name varies by AMI (e.g. /dev/xvda for Amazon Linux, /dev/sda1 for Ubuntu).

checks.message: Detailed monitoring not enabled
checks.context: Without detailed monitoring, CloudWatch metrics are only available at 5-minute intervals. Detailed monitoring provides 1-minute granularity, critical for detecting and responding to security incidents quickly. Note: detailed monitoring incurs additional CloudWatch charges.

checks.message: Instance launched with a public IP address
checks.context: Assigning a public IP makes the instance directly reachable from the internet. Automated scanners find open ports within minutes. Use a NAT gateway for outbound traffic and a load balancer for inbound, keeping instances in private subnets.

checks.message: Public IP assignment not explicitly disabled and will depend on subnet default
checks.context: Whether an instance gets a public IP depends on the subnet's auto-assign setting. If you intend this instance to be private, explicitly set --no-associate-public-ip-address rather than relying on the subnet default.

checks.message: Port open to the entire internet (0.0.0.0/0)
checks.context: Exposing ports to the world is one of the most common causes of breaches. Automated scanners find open ports within minutes of creation. Restrict to your IP or a known CIDR range.

checks.message: Port open to the entire internet via IPv6 (::/0)
checks.context: IPv6 wildcard rules are often overlooked but equally dangerous as 0.0.0.0/0. Any host on the internet can reach this port.

checks.message: Unrestricted outbound traffic allowed
checks.context: Allowing all outbound traffic makes it trivial for malware or a compromised instance to exfiltrate data or communicate with command-and-control servers. Restrict egress to only required destinations and ports.

checks.message: EBS volume created without encryption
checks.context: An unencrypted volume can be detached from a stopped instance and mounted elsewhere, giving full access to its contents. AWS KMS encryption adds no latency and costs nothing extra.

checks.message: Verify snapshot is not shared publicly after creation
checks.context: Snapshots shared with 'all' are publicly accessible to any AWS account. Run `ec2 describe-snapshot-attribute` after creation to confirm the snapshot is private.

checks.message: Snapshot being shared publicly with all AWS accounts
checks.context: A public snapshot exposes your disk image — including any secrets, credentials, or sensitive data on the volume — to every AWS account in the world. Sharing is done via --create-volume-permission Add=[{Group=all}].

checks.message: New security group created — ingress rules not yet defined
checks.context: Security groups are deny-by-default until you add rules. When you do, avoid 0.0.0.0/0 on sensitive ports (22, 3389, 3306). Use security group references instead of CIDRs where possible.

checks.message: Long-lived SSH key pair created
checks.context: Private keys committed to git repos or left in Downloads folders are a leading cause of cloud breaches. Consider EC2 Instance Connect or SSM Session Manager for SSH-free access instead.

checks.message: Ensure launch template enforces IMDSv2 and encrypted volumes
checks.context: Launch templates are reused at scale — a single insecure template can spawn hundreds of vulnerable instances. Bake in HttpTokens=required and EBS encryption now so every instance inherits them automatically.

checks.message: Enable VPC Flow Logs after creation
checks.context: Without flow logs you have zero visibility into network traffic — making it impossible to detect lateral movement, data exfiltration, or port scanning inside your VPC.

checks.message: Verify this subnet is not unintentionally public
checks.context: Subnets with auto-assign public IP enabled will expose every instance launched into them directly to the internet. Keep application and data tiers in private subnets behind a load balancer.

checks.message: Internet gateway created — ensure only public subnets route to it
checks.context: Attaching an IGW to a VPC and adding a default route in a subnet makes that subnet public. Verify your route tables so private subnets (databases, app servers) never have a 0.0.0.0/0 route pointing to this IGW.

checks.message: Elastic IP allocated — associate it promptly to avoid charges and exposure
checks.context: Unassociated Elastic IPs incur charges. More importantly, an EIP attached to a public instance bypasses NAT and exposes the instance directly. Ensure it's associated only to resources that genuinely need direct internet access.

checks.message: New NACL created — default denies all traffic until rules are added
checks.context: A custom NACL denies all inbound and outbound traffic by default. Ensure you add both inbound and outbound allow rules before associating it with a subnet, or you will break all connectivity to instances in that subnet.

checks.message: Ensure flow logs capture REJECT traffic for security analysis
checks.context: Flow logs set to ACCEPT-only miss blocked connection attempts — exactly the traffic that indicates port scanning or brute-force attacks. Use ALL or REJECT traffic type for security monitoring.

checks.message: Disabling termination protection on EC2 instance
checks.context: Removing termination protection makes the instance vulnerable to accidental or malicious deletion via terminate-instances. Only disable this immediately before a planned termination.

checks.message: AMI being shared publicly with all AWS accounts
checks.context: A public AMI exposes your machine image — including any baked-in secrets, application code, or configuration — to every AWS account in the world. Share only with specific trusted account IDs.

checks.message: Attaching an internet gateway enables public internet access for the VPC
checks.context: Once attached, any subnet with a route to the IGW becomes a public subnet. Instances with public IPs in those subnets become directly reachable from the internet. Verify this is intentional.

checks.message: AMI contains a full disk snapshot — ensure no secrets or credentials are baked in
checks.context: The AMI captures everything on the root and attached EBS volumes: SSH keys, environment files, application secrets, and credentials. If shared, all of that data is exposed to the recipient.

checks.message: Verify the new version enforces IMDSv2 and encrypted volumes — don't regress security
checks.context: A new launch template version can override security settings from the previous version. If the new version omits HttpTokens=required or EBS encryption, all future instances launched from it will be insecure.

checks.message: NAT gateways incur hourly charges and data processing fees — verify this is intentional
checks.context: A NAT gateway costs ~$0.045/hour plus $0.045/GB processed. For high-throughput workloads this can add up quickly. Ensure the NAT gateway is in a public subnet with a route to an internet gateway.

checks.message: Listing reserved instances on the marketplace is a financial commitment — verify pricing and terms
checks.context: Once listed, your reserved instances are available for purchase by other AWS customers. Misconfigured pricing or terms cannot be easily reversed. Verify the listing details carefully.

checks.message: Verify the route target is correct — a wrong route can expose private traffic or black-hole it
checks.context: A route to 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to an internet gateway makes the subnet public. A route pointing to the wrong NAT gateway, VPC peering, or transit gateway can send traffic to unintended destinations.

checks.message: New route tables have only a local route — associate subnets and add routes before use
checks.context: A route table without routes only allows local VPC traffic. Instances in subnets associated with it will have no internet or cross-VPC connectivity until routes are added.

checks.message: Removing the egress-only IGW cuts outbound IPv6 internet access for the VPC
checks.context: Instances using IPv6 for outbound connections (e.g., fetching updates, calling external APIs) will lose connectivity. This does not affect IPv4 traffic.

checks.message: Removing the internet gateway cuts all public internet connectivity for the VPC
checks.context: All instances relying on the IGW for outbound internet access or inbound public traffic will lose connectivity immediately. NAT gateways in public subnets also depend on the IGW.

checks.message: Deleting the key pair does not remove it from existing instances — but you lose the ability to connect to new ones
checks.context: Existing instances retain the public key. However, if you need to launch a replacement instance from the same AMI, you won't be able to SSH in without creating a new key pair first.

checks.message: Verify no Auto Scaling groups or launch configurations reference this template
checks.context: If an ASG references this template, new instance launches will fail. Existing running instances are not affected, but any scale-out or replacement will break.

checks.message: Deleting a route immediately breaks connectivity for traffic matching that destination
checks.context: If this route provides internet access (via NAT or IGW) or cross-VPC connectivity, deleting it instantly breaks all dependent services. Verify no active traffic uses this route.

checks.message: Verify no instances, ENIs, or other resources reference this security group
checks.context: AWS prevents deletion if the security group is in use, but referenced security groups in other groups' rules will become orphaned references. This can silently break network connectivity.

checks.message: Snapshot deletion is permanent — verify no AMIs or volumes depend on this snapshot
checks.context: If this snapshot is the backing store for an AMI, deleting it may make the AMI unusable. Verify dependencies before deleting.

checks.message: Deleting a VPC peering connection immediately cuts all cross-VPC traffic using it
checks.context: All routes pointing to this peering connection become black holes. Applications relying on cross-VPC communication will fail instantly. Verify both sides are prepared.

checks.message: Deleting a VPN gateway cuts all VPN connectivity to on-premises networks
checks.context: Any Site-to-Site VPN connections attached to this gateway are destroyed. On-premises applications relying on this VPN path will lose connectivity immediately.

checks.message: Fast snapshot restore incurs charges per AZ per snapshot — verify cost impact
checks.context: FSR is billed per minute per snapshot per AZ. Enabling it on many snapshots across multiple AZs can generate significant charges. Only enable for snapshots that need immediate full-performance volumes.

checks.message: Reboot causes temporary service disruption — verify these are not serving live traffic
checks.context: Unlike stop/start, a reboot preserves the public IP and instance store data. However, all in-flight requests are dropped and the instance is unreachable for 1-5 minutes during reboot.

checks.message: Stopping instances causes immediate service disruption — verify these are not production
checks.context: Stopped instances lose their public IP (unless Elastic IP), all data on instance store volumes, and any in-flight requests. Applications relying on these instances fail immediately.
